Recast member data down to the leaf layer, and back

Source: R/recast.R
recast_to_leaves.Rd

The two public halves of the from -> leaves -> to route: recast_to_leaves() projects member-keyed data DOWN to the leaf layer (one row per leaf), and recast_from_leaves() aggregates leaf-keyed data UP into a frame's members. Their composition is recast_scale(), and because the leaf rows are keyed by the leaf codes, recast_from_leaves(recast_to_leaves(data, a), b, target) recasts across two scales that share leaf codes.

Usage

recast_to_leaves(
  data,
  x,
  source = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  rule = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  attach_weight = TRUE,
  collect = NULL
)

recast_from_leaves(
  data,
  x,
  target,
  key = NULL,
  values = NULL,
  rule = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  na_rm = FALSE,
  na_action = c("drop", "error", "keep"),
  collect = NULL
)

Arguments

data

The data: for recast_to_leaves() keyed by member code at frame source; for recast_from_leaves() keyed by leaf codes.

x

The NestedScale the data is keyed in, or aggregated into.

source

to_leaves only: frame name the codes belong to. NULL (default) is inferred as in recast_scale().

key

The key column; defaults as in recast_scale().

values, rule

As in recast_scale().

weight

to_leaves: a declared weight column of x. from_leaves: the name of a column of data to weight by, so the weight may vary by identifier. NULL uses a weight column of the data if present, else the scale's declared weight.

attach_weight

to_leaves only: attach the weight column (default TRUE).

collect

For lazy inputs: materialise (TRUE) or return the query.

target

from_leaves only: target frame name.

na_rm

from_leaves only: read an NA value as "this member says nothing" rather than as an unknown that makes the whole group NA.

na_action

from_leaves only: what to do with leaves that have no code at target.

Value

recast_to_leaves(): one row per (leaf x identifier combination). recast_from_leaves(): one row per (member x identifier combination). Both in the input's class; lazy in, lazy out.

Details

Going down, extensive columns (rule "sum") are split across a member's leaves proportionally to the chosen weight so totals conserve; intensive columns are repeated. A weight column is attached by default so the return trip's "weighted_mean" reproduces the source weighting exactly.

Examples

s <- scale_example()
d <- data.frame(sector = c("P", "S"), capacity = c(10, 20))
leaves <- recast_to_leaves(d, s,
  source = "sector", rule = "sum",
  weight = "size"
)
head(leaves)
#>   item  capacity weight
#> 1   U1  1.000000    100
#> 2   U2  2.000000    200
#> 3   U3  3.000000    300
#> 4   U4  4.000000    400
#> 5   U5  9.090909    500
#> 6   U6 10.909091    600
recast_from_leaves(
  leaves, s,
  target = "class",
  rule = "sum",
  na_action = "keep"
)
#>   class capacity
#> 1    G1        3
#> 2    G2        7
#> 3    S1       20
#> 4  <NA>       NA
